Export outcomes for bayesma

Source: R/export.R
as_bayesma.Rd

Checks that the workbook holds what the chosen bayesma model needs and returns data in bayesma's input structure.

Usage

as_bayesma(
  data,
  outcome = NULL,
  ...,
  timepoint = NULL,
  model_type = c("two_stage", "one_stage"),
  measure = NULL,
  format = c("wide", "long"),
  estimate_means = c("none", "wan", "qe"),
  design_effect = c("apply", "ignore")
)

Arguments

data

An ma_data object or outcome data frame.

outcome

Outcome identifier(s), matched against outcome_id and then outcome_name. NULL keeps every outcome.

...

Unused; must be empty.

timepoint

Time point(s) to keep. NULL keeps every time point.

model_type

"two_stage" or "one_stage", as in bayesma's stage.

measure

Effect measure for every outcome. NULL uses each outcome's measure column.

format

"wide" or "long"; see Description.

estimate_means

For "MD" and "SMD": "none" (default) keeps studies as reported, so studies reporting only medians are flagged as incomplete; "wan" or "qe" first estimates missing means and SDs from medians, quartiles and ranges with convert_median_to_mean().

design_effect

"apply" (default) or "ignore"; see compute_effect_size().

Value

A data frame.

Details

  • format = "wide": one row per study for bayesma::bayesma(), with the outcome's own n_int/n_ctrl and the arm summaries named as bayesma's defaults (event_*, mean_*, sd_*, time_*, median_*, ...). For model_type = "two_stage", yi and sei are appended. Use study_var = study_id (or author with year_var = year) and, for model_type = "bc_jung", rob_var = rob_Overall. The reported sample sizes are kept; a design_effect column (see compute_design_effect()) is added for bayesma(design_effect = design_effect), and two-stage yi/sei already use the effective sample sizes.

  • format = "long": one row per arm for bayesma::bayesma_mv() (several outcomes), bayesma::bayesma_long() (several time points) or multi-arm models, with columns arm_id, events, n, mean, sd and exposure. Use arm_var = arm_id.

Studies with no summary data for an outcome (e.g. rows added by "Sync studies" for studies that did not report it) are left out of that outcome, with a message. Studies with partial data (e.g. a mean without an SD) are kept with a warning naming the missing fields; yi/sei are left empty where they cannot be calculated.

Several outcomes

With more than one outcome (or time point) in wide format, outcomes are placed side by side: one row per study, study details once, and each outcome's columns suffixed with its outcome_id (and time point, when an outcome has several), e.g. outcome_id_hosp_los, yi_hosp_los, sei_icu_los. Studies that did not report an outcome have empty cells for it. Each outcome uses its own measure unless measure is given. With a single outcome, columns keep their plain names (yi, sei, ...).
